items.reason: The clearest example of a priori justification asks for philosophical knowledge, not just an outlook.
Some unknowable questions do not reject the attainability of knowledge elsewhere.
Successful false theories remain possible under fallibilist scientific realism.
The vignette presupposes that a contextual feature changes what is appropriate.
Same morally relevant facts may conceal a tautological consistency claim.
Unqualified wording may accidentally deny atemporal abstract objects; do not classify presentism from it.
Possibility of abstract representation does not itself endorse an abstract-world ontology.
An evidential restriction on supernatural explanations is not a denial that supernatural reality exists.
A definition of determinism tests recognition of a definition rather than belief that the world is deterministic.
Evaluation of one wallet example confounds human-nature beliefs with standards of evidence.
